name: tmdb
readme_html:
TMDB for Kedi

Find a film by title and retrieve its director, release date, and runtime using TMDB's API. No movie IDs or MCP server configuration are needed.

Install

kedi add tmdb

Kedi installs httpx>=0.27,<1 into the Python environment running the command. Use Python 3.11-3.14 and a Kedi version with automatic Python dependency installation.

Credentials

Set TMDB_API_KEY to your TMDB API Read Access Token, not the shorter API key. The tool sends the token as a Bearer header. Obtain a token from your TMDB API settings.

For example, put this in a local .env beside your program when using the Kedi CLI:

TMDB_API_KEY=your-tmdb-read-access-token

Use from a model

> import: tmdb
> approval: allow
> use: movie_details

>> Look up Spirited Away using movie_details. Its director is [director: str], release year [year: int], and runtime [minutes: int] minutes.

= `{"director": director, "year": year, "minutes": minutes}`

Configure your generative model and its credentials separately. For example:

kedi movie_night.kedi --adapter-model google/gemini-3-flash-preview

The Google model requires GOOGLE_API_KEY and the pydantic-ai-slim[google] provider dependency. The package itself makes no model calls.

Call directly

> import: tmdb

= `movie_details("Dune", 1984)`

movie_details(title: str, year: int = 0) -> dict returns:

{
  "title": "Dune",
  "release_date": "1984-12-14",
  "runtime": 137,
  "directors": ["David Lynch"]
}

A call searches for the title and then requests the matching movie's details and credits. Exact title matches are preferred; the tool rejects missing or ambiguous results rather than picking an arbitrary movie. Supply a release year to distinguish remakes. Each HTTP request has a 10-second timeout. HTTP errors, rate limits, invalid responses, and timeouts propagate to the caller.
